citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Daily observation of the sheep to assess their health and well-being is not being done adequately, nor is there direct and
frequent communication with the attending veterinarian regarding their health problems.
An adult ram, black in color with a white-speckled head, was noted to be lying down, separated from the herd and when
he got up, he limped and did not bear weight on his left front leg. His movements were stiff and he appeared to move in a
manner that indicated pain. Both ears when inspected were drooping, thickened (approximately 5x+ in thickness), and
hard to the touch. The back side of the left ear had skin falling off and had an odor of decay. The ear was oozing and wet
in appearance with cloudy discharge, with dried grass, and dirt stuck inside the wound. The draining area is approximately
the entire backside of the ear. When asked about this animal, the licensee stated he had not noticed the ears and the
limping was first noticed that morning. This ram’s condition must be communicated to the attending veterinarian for
diagnosis and potential treatment options.
Failure to identify these issues and failing to maintain timely communication about those findings with the attending
veterinarian can lead to treatment delay, which may negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals. Each
exhibitor shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include daily observation of all animals to
assess their health and well-being as well as direct and frequent communication so that timely and accurate information
on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Additional Inspectors:
